Hi Ellie,

Hope you’re well — I’m reaching because the organizers at SaaS Summit West asked if Redwood and one of our customers would be willing to do a short customer spotlight panel at the conference on July 14. We’d love to highlight Novus Health’s work on deploying inference for clinical summarization and the measurable latency/cost improvements you saw after moving to Redwood’s Dedicated tier.

What we’re proposing: a 20–25 minute joint panel (Redwood + Novus) — ~10–12 min case highlight + brief live Q&A. We can accommodate remote participation, and there’s a modest speaker stipend to cover travel if you prefer to join in person.

If this sounds interesting, would you be open to:
- a quick 20-min coordination call next week to confirm audience and talking points
- sharing a 1-page snapshot of the Novus deployment you’re comfortable publicly discussing (we’ll draft and send for approval)

I’ve cc’d Marissa from our customer marketing team to help with the one-pager and logistics. I’m attaching a proposed agenda and our speaker guidelines so you can see the format.

Attachments: proposed_agenda.pdf, speaker_guidelines.docx

Thanks — happy to work around whatever level of public detail you’re comfortable with.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Hi Ellie — thanks for the quick note. Answers inline below and copied Marissa + Rachel to help with legal/logistics: 

1) Remote participation: yes, remote is totally fine. We’ll ask the session moderator to call on you for the live Q&A so it flows smoothly.
2) Stipend / travel: there is a modest speaker stipend; for full in-person attendance we can cover travel + 1 hotel night. If you present remotely, we can arrange an honorarium. Happy to confirm amounts in the speaker agreement.
3) Technical depth: the organizer prefers an outcomes-focused brief: the audience is a mix of engineering leads and platform owners. Suggested structure for Novus: 1–2 slides on the problem (scale/latency/cost), 2 slides on what you changed (model variants, Dedicated config, caching), 1 slide on measurable outcomes (p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens), then short Q&A. We’ll scrub any references to PHI or sensitive detail; Marissa will route anything that needs legal review.

I’ve attached the proposed agenda and speaker guidelines again. If you’re comfortable, I can draft the one-pager (Novus case snapshot) and send it back to you for sign-off — Marissa will lead that. I’ve also added a placeholder DocuSign link (we’ll swap in the official one once procurement confirms).

Attachments: proposed_agenda.pdf, speaker_guidelines.docx
Related link: https://tinyurl.com/saas-summit-2026-slot

If this works, can we book a 20-min sync Tue (Feb 24) or Wed (Feb 25)?

Best,
Soojin

Hi team — per Soojin’s request I pulled together a first-pass one-pager for Novus to approve. Draft below — I’ll drop a PDF once we’ve agreed on metrics to highlight.

Novus Health — Redwood Inference customer snapshot (DRAFT)
- Problem: Clinical summarization at scale — long seq lengths and strict latency SLAs for clinician UX
- Solution: Moved inference to Redwood Dedicated with KV caching + per-route batching, selected a quantized LLM variant for stable throughput
- Outcomes: ~45% reduction in average cost per 1k tokens, p95 latency improved from 720ms to ~320ms under production traffic, deployment supports burst to 300 concurrent sessions
- Suggested quotes: 
  • “Switching to Redwood reduced our cost and fixed jitter we were seeing at peak.” — VP Eng (quote to approve)

Questions for Novus to confirm (Ellie):
- Can you confirm the p95 and cost delta numbers above? If legal prefers ranges we can say “~300–350ms p95” and “~40–50% cost reduction.”
- Do you want us to mention any model names or keep it high-level?

Planned attachments once approved: novus-case-onepager.pdf, novus-headshot.jpg

Thanks — I can tighten copy after Ellie’s confirmation and then send for a final sign-off.
